## chatbot

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `minimal`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Assistant boilerplate that belongs to a chat window.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `certainly!`, `absolutely!`, `of course!` (sentence-initial) | cut |
| `I hope this helps`, `hope this helps` | cut |
| `great question`, `excellent question`, `good question` | cut |
| `feel free to reach out`, `feel free to ask`, `feel free to contact`, `feel free to let me know` | cut |
| `don't hesitate to` | cut |
| `let me know if you`, `let me know if there`, `let me know if that`, `let me know if this`, `let me know if it` | cut |
| `happy to help` | cut |
| `I'd be happy to`, `I would be happy to` | cut |
| `as an AI`, `as an AI language model` | cut |
| `as of my last update`, `as of my last training`, `as of my last knowledge`, `as of my latest update`, `as of my latest training`, `as of my latest knowledge`, `knowledge cutoff` | cut |
| `I don't have access to real-time` | cut |
| `As a language model` | cut |
| `I am an AI` | cut |
| `I'm just an AI` | cut |
| `As an assistant` | cut |
| `I cannot browse` | cut, state the limit |
| `I don't have personal opinions` | cut |
| `I'm unable to browse`, `verify this`, and the like | state what you can do |
| `please note that` | state the fact |
| `Kindly` + verb | imperative without "kindly" |

## closers

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Endings that restate the text instead of stopping.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Ultimately` (sentence-initial) | cut |
| `As we move forward`, `Moving forward` (sentence-initial) | cut |
| `in conclusion`, `in summary`, `to summarize`, `to sum up` | cut, end on the last fact |
| `at the end of the day`, `only time will tell`, `stay tuned`, `exciting times`, `happy coding`, `thank me later` | cut |
| `the future looks bright`, `the future is bright`, `the possibilities are endless` | cut |
| `one thing is certain`, `one thing is clear` | state it |
| `worth reading`, `worth a look`, `worth a read`, `worth exploring`, `worth checking out`, `worth your time` | say why |
| `the journey begins`, `the journey continues`, `the journey is just beginning`, `the adventure begins`, `the adventure continues`, `the adventure is just beginning` | cut |
| `the bottom line`, `the key takeaway`, `the takeaway here` | state it |
| `I look forward to`, `we look forward to` | cut, or state the next step and date |

## contrast

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT), Ryan Yannelli's house rules, and Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing.

Frames that define the subject by what it is not.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `it's not X, it's Y` (also `it is not`, `this is not`, `that's not`, with `just`, `only`, `about`, `merely`, or `simply` inside) | state the positive claim |
| `isn't about X, it's about Y` | state the positive claim |
| `not just X but Y` (also `not only`, `not merely`, `not simply`) | state Y |
| `X, not Y` as the tail of a sentence, up to 3 words after `not` | write the claim as "X does Y" |
| `less about X, more about Y` | state the positive claim |
| `instead of X, it's Y` | state the claim directly |
| `isn't X. It's Y.` | combine into one claim |

A bare `rather than` is not flagged: it is ordinary technical English. The cross-sentence form stops at a second negation, which the negative-parallelism pack owns.

## copula

Presets: `ryan`, `ste`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Verbs that interpret the subject instead of naming what it does.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `serves as`, `acts as`, `stands as`, `functions as` | is, or the literal action |
| `boasts` | has |
| `the source of truth` | say what reads it |
| `the key constraint` | name the constraint |
| `the path forward` | the next step, named |
| `this ensures` | say what happens |
| `plays a key role`, `plays a vital role`, `plays a critical role`, `plays a central role`, `plays a significant role`, `plays an important role` | say what it does |
| `designed to help`, `designed to ensure`, `designed to provide`, `designed to enable`, `designed to make` | say what it does |

State the fact instead of interpreting it.

## elegant-variation

Presets: `ryan`, `all`. Source: Fowler via Wikipedia:Elegant variation and Wikipedia:The problem with elegant variation.

Rotating synonyms for one referent instead of repeating the name.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `aforementioned` | name it again |
| `the eponymous` | name it directly |
| `self-titled` | name it directly |
| `the titular` | name it directly |
| `of the same name` | name it directly, or cut |
| Rotating synonyms for one referent instead of repeating the name. | `minWords = 200`, `minSynonyms = 3` |

The counting half needs 200 words and three synonyms from one cluster, each used once. Repeating a word turns the paragraph off.

## false-ranges

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: tropes.fyi directory and the agent-toolkit signs-of-ai-writing mirror.

A "from X to Y" span whose endpoints share no real scale.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `everything from X to Y` | list the specific items |
| `anything from X to Y` | list the specific items |
| `runs the gamut from X to Y` | name the actual range |
| `the full spectrum of X from A to B` | name the actual range |
| `from A to B to C` | split into a list |

A plain two-point range stays unflagged, so numeric and version ranges pass. The chained form skips a span that holds a digit or a parenthesis, and skips a third `to` that opens a purpose clause, so `from 0 to 1000 to pick a victim` and `from left to right to reduce the list` stay clean. Only the marked forms and chained word spans report.

## filler

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Openers and asides that carry no fact.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `honestly` (sentence-initial) | cut |
| `genuinely`, `truly`, `quite frankly`, `to be honest`, `real talk`, `at its core`, `here's the thing` | cut |
| `let's be clear`, `let's be honest` | cut |
| `a genuine improvement`, `a genuine step`, `a genuine shift`, `a genuine change`, `a genuine concern`, `a genuine interest` | cut |
| `it's important to note`, `it's important to remember`, `it's important to understand`, `it is important to note`, `it is important to remember`, `it is important to understand` | state the point |
| `worth flagging`, `worth mentioning`, `worth remembering` | state the point |
| `let's unpack`, `let's dive in`, `let's explore`, `let's take a look`, `let's break this down`, `let's break it down`, `let's examine`, `let's get started` | start with the point |
| `straightforward` | cut, or say what the steps are |
| `a powerful example` | the example |
| `this highlights`, `this speaks to` | state the fact |
| `the broader takeaway` | state it |
| `a reminder that`, `a reminder of`, `a stark reminder that`, `a stark reminder of`, `a powerful reminder that`, `a powerful reminder of`, `a timely reminder that`, `a timely reminder of`, `an important reminder that`, `an important reminder of` | state the fact |
| `I recently had the pleasure of` | say what happened |
| `whether you're X or Y` | name the audience or cut |

## formatting

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT), Ryan Yannelli's house rules, Pangram signs-of-ai-writing.

Emoji and bold runs used as structure.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| an emoji in a heading | remove |
| an emoji ending a line | remove |
| an emoji starting a line | remove |
| an emoji before a colon | remove |

A code check in ai-patterns.mjs reports three or more bold spans in one paragraph or list item; no pattern row covers it. The pack applies one scope to every pattern, so the line-initial emoji rule also runs on commit messages and flags a gitmoji prefix such as a sparkle before `feat:`. A repo on that convention puts the glyph in `allowList.patterns`, or ships its own `formatting` pack with a `scope` that leaves out `commit`.

## hedging

Presets: `ryan`, `ste`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Qualifiers that leave the claim unowned.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Note that` (sentence-initial) | cut, state the fact |
| `perhaps`, `arguably` | cut, or commit |
| `may eventually`, `could eventually` | say when |
| `could potentially`, `may potentially`, `might potentially`, `might possibly`, `could possibly` | can, or cut |
| `to be clear`, `in general` | cut |
| `keep in mind` | cut, state the fact |
| `generally`, `typically` | cut, or name the exception |
| `in some cases`, `in many cases`, `in most cases` | name the case |
| `somewhat`, `to some extent` | cut, or measure |
| `it could be argued`, `it could be said`, `it may be argued`, `it may be said`, `it might be argued`, `it might be said` | state the claim |
| `potentially` (bare) | cut |

## inflation

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: avoid-ai-writing by Conor Bronsdon (MIT) and Ryan Yannelli's house rules.

Wording that makes a change sound larger than it is.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `marks a significant`, `marks a major`, `marks a new`, `marks a turning` | state what happened |
| `represents a significant`, `represents a major`, `represents a fundamental` | state what changed |
| `a significant step forward`, `a major step towards`, `a bold step toward`, `a big step forward`, `step forward for` | state what changed |
| `turning point`, `sea change`, `paradigm shift`, `game-changer`, `game-changing`, `watershed moment` | state what changed |
| `groundbreaking` | name the prior art it beats |
| `first of its kind` | cite the search |
| `revolutionary`, `revolutionize`, `revolutionizes`, `revolutionized` | describe the change |
| `the future of` | cut |
| `unprecedented` | name the precedent, or cut |
| `redefine the`, `redefine how`, `redefine what`, `redefines the`, `redefines how`, `redefines what`, `reshape the`, `reshapes the`, `reshaping the` | describe the change |
| `real utility`, `actual value`, `genuine impact`, `true change`, `real results` | drop the adjective |
| `despite challenges`, `despite these challenges`, `despite the challenges` | name the challenge |
| `continues to thrive`, `remains resilient` | cite the number |

## lexical-diversity

Presets: `statistical`, `all`.

Flags text that reuses the same words instead of varying vocabulary.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| Flags text that reuses the same words instead of varying vocabulary. | `minWords = 150`, `minRatio = 0.55`, `segment = 100`, `tailSegment = 50` |

Mean segmental type-token ratio over 100-word segments. Direction of the academic signal is contested, so it stays out of the ryan preset.

## negative-parallelism

Presets: `default`, `ryan`, `technical`, `all`. Source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, WikiProject AI Cleanup catchphrases, tropes.fyi, refine.so.

A chain of two or more negated clauses resolved by one affirmation.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Not X. Not Y. Just Z.` | state the one claim |
| `no X, no Y, just Z` | state the one claim |
| `not X, not Y, but Z` | state the one claim |
| `no X, no Y. Just Z.` | state the one claim |
| `isn't X. It's not Y. It's Z.` | state the one claim |

The contrast pack owns the single "not X, it's Y" pair. This pack fires only on two or more stacked negations before the resolution.

## outline-conclusion

Presets: `ryan`, `all`. Source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing (outline-like conclusions) and tropes.fyi fractal summaries.

A closing paragraph that re-lists the section headings instead of adding a new fact.

| Flagged | Fix |
|---|---|
| A closing paragraph that re-lists the section headings instead of adding a new fact. | `minWords = 300`, `minHeadings = 3`, `minOverlap = 3`, `minRatio = 0.6`, `smallDoc = 4`, `maxParagraphWords = 120` |

Needs 300 words, three headings, a closing paragraph that echoes three section titles, and a restatement cue. A closing paragraph that adds a new fact passes.
